findings.title: Feature-flagged TableWidgetVisualization renders hardcoded empty data
findings.body: In `tableResultComponent`, when the `use-table-widget-visualization` organization feature is enabled, the new branch renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{ data: [], meta: { fields: {}, units: {} } }} />` — completely ignoring the actual query results (`result.data`, `fields`, `eventView`, etc.) that the existing `StyledSimpleTableChart` path uses. `columns={[]}` also means no column headers are generated (the component's fallback of deriving columns from `meta.fields` gets an empty object too). Any organization that has this feature flag turned on will see every table widget on dashboards render as an empty table with no rows and no headers, instead of their data. The new visualization needs to be wired to the real table results before the flag can be enabled, or this branch should not ship.

findings.title: Truthy check on custom cell renderer discards valid falsy React nodes
findings.body: In `renderDefaultBodyCell` (and identically in `renderDefaultHeadCell` at line 32), the override is applied via `const cell = renderTableBodyCell?.(...); if (cell) { return cell; }`. The documented contract (in `tableWidgetVisualization.tsx` and the stories) is that returning `undefined` from a custom renderer triggers the fallback. With a truthiness check, a custom renderer that returns other valid falsy React nodes — `null` (to intentionally render nothing), `0`, or `''` — will be silently discarded and replaced by the default field renderer. This means a custom body/head cell renderer cannot render an empty cell. The check should be `if (cell !== undefined)` to match the documented contract.

findings.title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion check uses truthiness and age allows negatives
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` rejects only when `self.initial_data.get("age")` is truthy (and `validate_age` mirrors this for `timestamp`). A report containing both `timestamp` and `age: 0` passes validation even though the intent is that the two fields are mutually exclusive, because `0` is falsy. `age: 0` is a legitimate value for a report delivered immediately. Additionally, the `age` field is declared as `serializers.IntegerField(required=False)` with no `min_value`, while `timestamp` has `min_value=0`, so negative ages are accepted. Use `"age" in self.initial_data` (and add `min_value=0` to `age`) so the spec constraint is actually enforced.

findings.title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) misaligns IDs with nodestore data when entries are missing
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` builds pairs with `zip(error_ids, events.values())` and filters with `if data is not None`. `nodestore.backend.get_multi()` returns a dict keyed by node_id that omits entries whose data is missing (e.g., expired events). When any entry is dropped, `events.values()` is shorter than `error_ids`, so the zip shifts: an error ID gets paired with a *different* event's data, and the trailing IDs are silently dropped — the `if data is not None` filter cannot realign them. The result is `ErrorEvent` objects whose `id` does not correspond to their `title`/`message`/`timestamp`. Today `id` is not consumed downstream (only title/message/timestamp reach the Seer prompt), so the visible impact is latent, but the mapping is incorrect and any future use of `id` (and any debugging of these payloads) will be wrong. Iterate `node_ids` and look up `events.get(node_id)` instead.
